All three references are open in your browser and left running:

**1. Figure reference (Pinterest pin)**
- Link: https://www.pinterest.com/pin/42150946507920702/
- Pin title: "figure drawing reference photos references" — it's a photo-based full-body figure reference (real person, clear pose), which is much easier to sketch from than a sketch/anatomy diagram. Tip for a beginner: start with a light "line of action" through the figure's spine, then add the big shapes (head, torso, limbs) before any detail.

**2. 1500s English one-room hut (image source page)**
- Link: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Cruck_Cottage,_Upper_Farringdon_02.jpg
- What it is: "Cruck Cottage, Church Road, Upper Farringdon, Hampshire, England — 15th century and later, Grade II* listed" (photo by Simon Burchell, 2019, CC BY-SA 4.0, free to use with credit). This is a genuine cruck-frame timber cottage from exactly the period you want — a compact, single-room, thatched hut with the distinctive curved "A-frame" timbers, which makes it very drawable: basically a few leaning lines + a roof.

**3. Angry cat mood reference (Bored Panda)**
- Exact page title: "40 Times People Just Had To Snap A Pic Of Their Angry, But Cute Cats"
- Link: https://www.boredpanda.com/cute-angry-cats/
- A 40-photo collection of grumpy/irritated cat faces — great for exaggerating expressions. The recurring "angry cat" cues are easy to copy: flattened/airplane ears, narrowed eyes, bared teeth, bristled whiskers.

**How they fit together in one simple sketch idea:**
Draw the cruck hut as your background — keep it loose, just the A-frame timbers, a thatched roof, one door and a low smoke haze from the central hearth. In front of the door, sketch your figure as a 1500s villager (a simple cloak/tunic over the reference pose is enough to sell the period) — maybe crouched or leaning in the doorway. At their feet, add one small cat with the exaggerated Bored Panda face: ears pinned back, eyes narrowed, teeth showing, tail bristled. The story sells itself — the person just kicked a bucket of water / stepped on the tail / dropped the fish — and the grumpy cat gives the whole scene its mood. For a beginner, that's the whole recipe: one simple building shape, one gesture figure, one big expressive face. Keep it all in loose pencil lines and you'll have a charming little scene in under 30 minutes.

All three tabs are left open for you to work from.
